overview: The Marinids made Fez a royal capital and sponsored an urban culture of learning, worship, commerce and craftsmanship. Their new town stood beside the older medina, creating a capital with complementary royal and civic spaces.

items.text: Fez Jedid was founded in 1276 beside Fez el-Bali. It included the palace, fortifications, military headquarters and residential districts.
Madrasas and mosques are among the principal monuments associated with the city's Marinid flourishing in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries.
Fondouks, houses and fountains belonged to the capital's urban fabric alongside royal and religious buildings.
Fez's architecture brought local skills into conversation with influences from Andalusia and other African and eastern centers. Its craft traditions continued beyond any one dynasty.
